_: The board rules both readers implement, as cases rather than as code. scripts/dev.py and
(ADR 0013, ADR 0055): the columns they build are deliberately different and one of them is Swift
in an app that must stay dependency-free. What is shared is the RULE, and this file is where it lives.
This file is a REGISTRY, not only a fixture. Both suites fail when a rule named here has no binding
on their side, so adding a rule to one reader and not the other is what breaks the build — which is
the failure ADR 0013 left to whoever remembered, and nobody did (the install root, #88).
To add a rule: add it here with its cases, then bind it in tests/state/test_board_conformance.py
and in apps/desk/DeskCore/Tests/DeskCoreTests/BoardConformanceTests.swift. Both fail until you do.
Cases pin AGREEMENT, not correctness. priority_rank returns the first matching label rather than the
best one, so an issue labelled P1,P0 ranks 1 in both readers; that is recorded below as it behaves.

branch_matches.what: The branch names that speak for issue N: gh-N-…, N-…, N, or any/N-… — never gh-N0-…

closed_issues.what: The issues a pull request body CLAIMS. Prose mentioning #N is not a claim on N.

priority_rank.what: P0..P3 rank 0..3; unlabelled ranks 4, AFTER P3, because unprioritised is not urgent.

slice_rank.what: `slice N` in a title is a dependency statement, so N+1 never precedes N. No slice sorts last.

is_decomposed_epic.what: An epic whose CHECKLIST still has an open child is already decomposed: offer a child instead.

order_next.what: Priority, then slice, then the issue ignored longest, then number. Returns the numbers in order.

agent_prompt.what: The prompt a task's agent is started with. A task names itself only while it has no branch.
